_comment: BT-4485: the types whose values cross beamtalk_erlang_proxy unchanged, so an inline FFI call may skip the proxy. Rust: native_type_registry ffi_result_passes_unchanged / ffi_arg_passes_unchanged must accept exactly the listed types and reject the not_proven ones. Erlang: beamtalk_erlang_proxy_tests checks every sample (an Erlang expression) passes through unchanged, and every arg sample passes one of arg_runtime_guards (the erlang BIFs a direct call checks each argument with at run time; any other value, such as a tagged String, a charlist or a non-binary bitstring, falls back to the proxy; a String or Binary typed arg is checked with arg_binary_guard (is_binary) as well, and a Dictionary typed arg with arg_map_guard (is_map, BT-4770: the stock-mode unwrap is shallow and a map is not a tagged String, so a map reaches the callee unchanged); both kinds of call site take a class-variable snapshot for the badarg retry). A '#name' type is a Symbol singleton.
_comment_inline_result: BT-4762: a stock-mode call whose spec is Result(V, _) builds the Result at the call site (beamtalk_result:from_tagged_tuple/1) when the raw result is {ok, V} or {error, R} with a non-list payload, or the bare ok, and otherwise hands the already-returned value to coerce_ffi_result/3. Rust: V must be in result_passthrough, or Dynamic (BT-4770: a spec type variable such as maps:find/2's Value; the run-time not is_list test makes the shape correct for a payload of any type, lists included, as the samples show); inline_result_value_not_proven lists types it rejects. Erlang: every sample must come out of the inline shape exactly as coerce_ffi_result(M, Sample, stock) builds it.
